title: Add TTFT/TPOT threshold profiles for FP8/INT8 kernel canaries (per-SKU baselines + noise suppression)
author: Allison Grant
description: Context: As part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint, we’re enabling quantized kernel modes behind flags and rolling out via perf canary. The existing canary gating uses a single threshold policy that was tuned on baseline (FP16/BF16) runs and has been noisy for quantized modes (especially when sample sizes are small or when the scheduler mix shifts TTFT/TPOT differently). This PR introduces explicit threshold profiles for quantized kernels and per-SKU baselines so we can gate safely and reduce false positives while still catching real regressions. Summary of changes: (1) Add threshold profiles keyed by kernel_mode (baseline|fp8|int8) and sku (h100|a100|l4) with separate TTFT/TPOT constraints and minimum sample requirements. (2) Add noise suppression: a small-sample guardrail, robust aggregation using trimmed mean for p95 deltas, and an EWMA-based stability check that prevents flip-flopping when the signal is borderline. (3) Add a per-SKU baseline registry: baseline references are pinned by (model, sku, region, traffic_profile) so the canary compares fp8/int8 vs the correct baseline cohort rather than a global default. (4) Add explicit “capacity/variance” classification: if GPU clocks are not locked or if variance exceeds the configured bound, canary emits a WARN and does not auto-rollback (still pages on-call if error rate spikes). Default policies included (initial cut): H100 fp8 is allowed tighter TPOT deltas but slightly looser TTFT due to known launch/scheduler interactions in mixed workloads; A100 int8 is looser on TPOT until we finish shape guardrails coverage; L4 has stricter min-sample and longer evaluation window to smooth bursty workloads. Config format: new YAML profiles under config/threshold_profiles/ with schema validation in CI. Example snippet (illustrative only): profile: quantized_h100_fp8; ttft_p95_delta_pct_max: 6; tpot_p95_delta_pct_max: 3; min_requests: 2000; ewma_alpha: 0.2; trimmed_mean_pct: 10. Operational notes: This PR does NOT change any runtime flags. It only changes how perf-canary evaluates telemetry deltas when kernel_mode is fp8/int8. Rollback behavior: auto-rollback triggers remain enabled only when (a) min_requests met, (b) stability check passes (not high variance), and (c) delta breaches the configured bound for 2 consecutive windows. Otherwise we emit a blocking canary failure (no rollout progression) but do not auto-flip flags. Follow-ups: (a) once ENG-7428 matrix runs are complete we should tighten H100 fp8 TTFT; (b) add model-family overrides for known long-context TTFT sensitivity; (c) wire in the new metrics dimensions (model/gpu/kernel_mode) after runtime PR lands (tracked in ENG-7427/PR-19934 in monorepo).
commits: Add threshold profile schema + loader (validation, defaults, docs)
Introduce per-SKU baseline registry and cohort keying
Implement noise suppression (min sample, trimmed mean, EWMA stability)
Add quantized profiles (H100 FP8, A100 INT8, L4 INT8) + tests
Update evaluator output formatting and runbook notes
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes: The auto-rollback guardrails look good. Two questions: (1) what’s the behavior when sample size is met but variance is high? (2) can we ensure this doesn’t block non-quantized rollouts? I don’t want a global gating change that surprises us.

Allison Grant (author): (1) If variance > variance_max (computed from baseline window + current window), we classify the result as UNSTABLE and do not auto-rollback; we still stop progression and mark the canary as failed so on-call looks. (2) Non-quantized uses the existing default profile; the new profiles are selected only when kernel_mode tag matches fp8|int8. I added a unit test to ensure baseline profile remains the default when kernel_mode missing.

Noah Patel: The EWMA stability check is a good addition, but I’m concerned about the trimmed mean on p95 deltas — are we trimming across shards or across time windows? Also: can you link to the rationale from the sprint plan/variance investigation?

Allison Grant (author): Trim happens across time windows within the evaluation interval (we keep N windows, compute delta per window, then trim top/bottom 10% before aggregating). We don’t trim across shards; shards are already aggregated upstream. I added a comment + doc section and linked the approach to ENG-7429 notes in Linear.

Irene Choi: Please include explicit SKUs as they appear in fleet labels. Our H100 label is "h100-sxm" and "h100-pcie" in some regions. Can the profile system map both to "h100" without copy/pasting config?
Allison Grant (author): Added sku_aliases: [h100-sxm, h100-pcie] support in schema and mapped both to canonical "h100". Same for a100-80gb vs a100-40gb (canonical "a100"). Tests included.

Marcus Reed: For TTFT vs TPOT, the profile has TTFT looser than TPOT. That matches what we saw, but we should cap absolute TTFT delta in ms too; percent deltas can blow up on low-latency regions. Can we add an optional absolute bound?

Allison Grant (author): Added optional ttft_p95_delta_ms_max and tpot_p95_delta_ms_max fields. Set defaults only for L4 (since percent was too sensitive in our synthetic runs). Left H100/A100 on percent-only for now.
Rafael Mendes: Approved once the sku alias mapping lands.
Rafael Mendes: Looks good now. Approved.
release_notes: Perf-canary: Added quantized-kernel threshold profiles (FP8/INT8) with per-SKU baselines and noise suppression. Improves canary signal quality and reduces false-positive rollbacks during quantized rollouts.
